correctness.rationale: The proof uses an independent row-cycle upper bound 3s and a balanced three-band construction of exactly 3s vertices. The numeric inequalities q>=s+1 and 2(ceil(n/3)+s-1)<=n follow by all three residues and hold in the stated domain. Distinct-band pairs have a shortest cyclic arc across an empty gap and an unselected vertical switch; same-band pairs have explicit geodesics. All pairs are covered, including ties and the boundary n=6s-6. The embedded checker independently constructs paths and performs obstruction-aware BFS on 360 parameter pairs; finite checks only support, do not replace, the infinite proof.

broader_coverage.reasoning: The long-path theorem has circumference n<=s+1; here n>=6s-6>s+1 for every s>=3, so the earlier theorem cannot imply equality. A conjecture, even stronger in stated scope, is not a prior proof. The existing upper bound alone is insufficient; this finding supplies the matching constructions on an infinite two-parameter subregion.

value.rationale: The source explicitly conjectures equality with a two-factor upper bound for all large cycle circumferences and leaves the cylinder case open. The new three-band gap-switching lemma proves equality for unbounded s and n, not a fixed small example or numerical improvement. The theorem gives a uniform, reproducible optimal construction with a precise arithmetic feasibility regime; it is not inferred from the prior upper bound. It does not claim to solve the remaining boundary or classify all optimum sets.
